material_systems.name: Acrylic Stain-Blocking Exterior Primer for Wood Windows
material_systems.description: 100% acrylic exterior stain-blocking primer for previously painted wood window surfaces where existing paint has failed or peeled, exposing bare wood. Primary RP primer for exposed wood areas on SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT and SS_EXT_PEELING conditions. Spot prime when bare area <30%; full prime when bare area >=30% or SS_EXT_PEELING. Not used on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (skip prime) or SS_EXT_CHALKING (use chalk-binding instead). Previously painted substrate absorbs less than NC bare wood -- higher coverage per gallon than NC primer.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec EXT Primer
PPG Sun Proof Exterior Latex Primer
products.notes: Standard acrylic primer for bare wood areas on exterior windows. Seals exposed wood grain including end-grain at sash edges and sill nose. For spot priming (bare <30%), apply to scraped/sanded bare areas only. For full prime (bare >=30% or SS_EXT_PEELING), apply full surface after complete scrape and feather-edge sanding. QT5 requires 2 coats primer (see COMPAT_XWRP_012).

prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime scraped bare areas; full prime if bare >=30%
prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_PEELING: full surface prime after heavy scrape to sound substrate

material_systems.notes: Reuses existing system from SF_TRIM_EXT_RP pattern (SYS_EXT_TRRP_PRIMER_ACRYLIC). Same product family, adapted for window EA-based coverage model. Window profiles (sash rabbets, muntin intersections) require thorough coverage in recessed areas.

material_systems.name: Chalk-Binding Conditioner Primer for Exterior Windows
material_systems.description: Low-viscosity chalk-binding conditioner primer that penetrates and binds loose chalk residue on exterior window surfaces. MANDATORY for SS_EXT_CHALKING regardless of cladding type. Full surface application required -- chalk binding must be uniform. Apply after power wash and 24-48 hour dry time. Higher material consumption than standard acrylic primer due to aggressive absorption by chalk residue. Heavy chalk on south/west elevations = lower end of coverage range.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Multi-Purpose Primer
products.notes: MANDATORY for chalking surfaces. Penetrates and binds loose chalk particles left after power wash. Do NOT skip -- topcoat adhesion failure guaranteed without chalk-binding step. Applies to all cladding types (wood, aluminum-clad, vinyl-clad) in chalking state. Full surface application required. QT5 requires 2 coats (see COMPAT_XWRP_012).

material_systems.notes: Reuses existing system from SF_TRIM_EXT_RP pattern (SYS_EXT_TRRP_PRIMER_CHALKBIND). Same product family. Chalk-binding is thicker bodied -- lower coverage per gallon than standard acrylic primer.

material_systems.name: Corrosion-Inhibiting DTM Spot Primer for Exposed Aluminum Cladding
material_systems.description: Industrial-grade corrosion-inhibiting direct-to-metal (DTM) primer for exposed aluminum cladding areas on exterior windows where paint has failed or peeled. Spot prime on bare aluminum areas only -- not full surface unless extensive failure exposes large aluminum area. Mandatory for adhesion on aluminum substrate. Must be applied over mechanical bonding profile (180-220 grit scuff-sand on bare aluminum). In RP context, exposed aluminum occurs at paint failure points (sash bottom rail, frame joints, sill); NC primes full surface.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Insl-X Aqua Lock Plus
products.notes: MANDATORY on exposed bare aluminum. Corrosion-inhibiting formula prevents oxidation under topcoat. Must scuff-sand bare aluminum with 180-220 grit before application. Spot prime exposed areas -- not full window surface unless extensive aluminum exposure. Same product as NC SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_CORROSION, applied in spot/selective mode for RP.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime exposed aluminum areas after scuff-sand
prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_PEELING: spot prime all exposed aluminum areas; full prime if extensive failure

material_systems.notes: Reuses existing DTM primer from NC exterior window spec (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_CORROSION). In RP, applied as spot primer on exposed aluminum only rather than full surface. Coverage profile uses COV_XWRP_PRIMER_DTM_SPOT (EA-based, fraction of total window surface).

material_systems.name: PVC Bonding Spot Primer for Exposed Vinyl Cladding
material_systems.description: Specialized PVC bonding primer for exposed vinyl cladding areas on exterior windows where paint has failed or peeled. MANDATORY for adhesion on vinyl substrate -- standard acrylic and alkyd primers will NOT bond to vinyl. Spot prime bare vinyl areas. Vinyl is non-porous, so bonding primer provides mechanical grip through chemical adhesion promotion. Must clean vinyl surface before application (no sanding required for bonding primer). Recoat within 1 week or primer loses flexibility.

products.notes: MANDATORY on exposed bare vinyl. Standard primers will NOT adhere to vinyl -- peeling within 6-12 months guaranteed. Clean vinyl surface before application. Spot prime exposed areas. Recoat window within 1 week of priming or bonding primer loses flexibility and becomes brittle. Same product as NC SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_BONDING_PVC, applied in spot mode for RP.

prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT: spot prime exposed vinyl areas after cleaning
prime_scope_by_state.SS_EXT_PEELING: spot prime all exposed vinyl areas; full prime if extensive failure

material_systems.notes: Reuses existing PVC bonding primer from NC exterior window spec (SYS_EXT_WIN_PRIMER_BONDING_PVC). In RP, applied as spot primer on exposed vinyl only. Coverage profile uses COV_XWRP_PRIMER_PVC_SPOT (EA-based, fraction of total window surface).

material_systems.name: Standard Acrylic Exterior Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Standard production 100% acrylic exterior enamel for QT3 window repaint. UV-resistant formula for exterior exposure. Hard enamel for thermal expansion/contraction cycling. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Once surface is prepped and primed, finish application is identical to NC. 2 coats standard at QT3.

products.notes: Standard exterior trim enamel. UV-resistant hard enamel for thermal cycling. Non-yellowing. Water cleanup. Latex topcoat on existing paint -- monitor for blocking on operable window sash contact surfaces. 1/16-inch glass lap for weather seal on final coat.

material_systems.notes: Standard production system for QT3 exterior window RP. Satin is default; semi-gloss available at QT3 per exterior sheen rules. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion on product selection.

material_systems.name: Modified Urethane Exterior Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Premium urethane-modified acrylic or waterborne alkyd exterior enamel for QT4 window repaint. Superior flow, leveling, and hardness. Enhanced UV and moisture resistance. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away. Blocking resistant -- ideal for operable window sashes. Extended cure time (7+ days full hardness in exterior conditions) -- keep sashes ajar during cure. 2 coats standard.

products.product_type: Urethane-modified acrylic / waterborne alkyd exterior enamel
products.notes: Premium exterior enamel. Superior flow and leveling. Harder cured film than standard acrylic. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away. Blocking resistant -- ideal for operable window sash contact surfaces. Extended exterior cure time (7-14 days depending on weather). Keep sashes ajar until fully cured.

material_systems.notes: Premium residential standard for QT4 exterior window RP. Semi-gloss is traditional/default exterior window sheen at this tier. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion.

material_systems.name: Premium Acrylic-Urethane Exterior Trim Enamel
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic-urethane enamel for superior exterior window repaint at QT5. Maximum durability, excellent leveling, hardest film. Maximum UV and moisture resistance. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away. Best blocking resistance of any waterborne system. Sands easily between coats for QT5 interstage protocol. 2 coats standard.

products.notes: Maximum durability. Excellent leveling. Hardest film. SHORT working time -- apply, tip once, walk away. Emerald Urethane is an acrylic-urethane enamel, NOT a waterborne alkyd. Best blocking resistance -- optimal for operable sashes. Sands easily between coats. Gloss available only at this tier.

material_systems.notes: Premium/custom home standard for QT5 exterior window RP. Gloss available only at this tier. Material systems are recommendations -- contractor has discretion.

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_S.notes: Small window: ~10 SF painted surface equivalent. Previously painted substrate absorbs less primer than bare wood -- higher coverage than NC COV_XWIN_PRIMER (425 SF/gal). Spot prime applies to scraped bare areas only (typically 15-40% of window surface at FAIR/POOR condition).

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_M.notes: Medium window: ~16 SF painted surface equivalent (calibration baseline). Previously painted substrate. Spot prime or full prime depending on bare percentage and state severity.

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_L.notes: Large window: ~25 SF painted surface equivalent. Includes bay/bow window assemblies. TDL muntins add ~20% surface area.

coverage_profiles.notes: Acrylic primer on previously painted exterior window surfaces. Higher coverage (425 SF/gal) than NC bare-wood primer (375 SF/gal COV_XWIN_PRIMER) because previously painted substrate is less absorptive. Window profiles (sash rabbets, muntin intersections, frame moldings) have recessed areas requiring thorough coverage.
assumptions: Previously painted substrate -- lower absorption than bare wood
Medium window: ~16 SF painted surface equivalent
Size bucket and muntin modifiers affect EA-to-SF conversion but not SF/gal coverage rate
Spot prime covers 15-40% of window surface (condition-dependent)

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_S.notes: Chalk-binding primer on chalking small window. Full surface application required. Lower coverage due to chalk residue absorption. Heavy chalk (south/west elevation) = lower end of range.

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_M.notes: Chalk-binding primer on chalking medium window. Full surface. Low-viscosity formula penetrates chalk layer aggressively -- expect higher material consumption than standard primer.

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_L.notes: Chalk-binding primer on chalking large window. Full surface. Highest material consumption per window due to large surface area and chalk absorption.

coverage_profiles.notes: Chalk-binding primer coverage is significantly lower than standard acrylic (275 vs 425 SF/gal) due to chalk residue absorption. Full surface application required on all chalking windows -- binding must be uniform. Follows SF_TRIM_EXT_RP coverage pattern (COV_TRRP_PRIMER_CHALKBIND at 275 SF/gal).
assumptions: Full surface application mandatory -- chalk binding must be uniform
Power wash first to remove loose chalk; primer binds remaining residue
Chalk severity drives coverage range: heavy chalk = low end, light chalk = high end
Applies to all cladding types in chalking state

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_S.notes: DTM spot primer on small aluminum-clad window. Spot priming exposed aluminum only -- typical bare exposure is 10-30% of window surface at failure points (sash bottom rail, frame joints).

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_M.notes: DTM spot primer on medium aluminum-clad window. Spot area varies widely by condition severity. Coverage rate per SF is consistent (375 SF/gal on non-porous aluminum).

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_L.notes: DTM spot primer on large aluminum-clad window. Larger window = more potential bare area, but spot coverage is still a fraction of total surface.

coverage_profiles.notes: DTM spot priming on exposed aluminum cladding. Coverage expressed per EA based on typical bare exposure area (10-30% of window surface). SF/gal rate matches NC full-surface DTM (375 SF/gal) because aluminum substrate is consistent. Wide EA-per-gallon range reflects condition severity variation.
assumptions: Spot priming bare aluminum areas only -- not full window surface
Typical bare exposure: 10-30% of total window surface at failure points
Aluminum is non-porous -- consistent coverage per SF regardless of state
Must scuff-sand bare aluminum (180-220 grit) before DTM primer application

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_S.notes: PVC bonding spot primer on small vinyl-clad window. Vinyl is non-porous -- highest coverage of any primer in this spec. Spot priming exposed vinyl only.

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_M.notes: PVC bonding spot primer on medium vinyl-clad window. Non-porous vinyl surface = consistent coverage. Spot area varies by condition severity.

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_L.notes: PVC bonding spot primer on large vinyl-clad window. Larger window = more potential bare area.

coverage_profiles.notes: PVC bonding spot primer on exposed vinyl cladding. Highest coverage of any primer in this spec (400 SF/gal) because vinyl is non-porous. Coverage consistent regardless of condition severity. Follows SF_TRIM_EXT_RP pattern (COV_TRRP_PRIMER_BONDING at 400 SF/gal).
assumptions: Vinyl is non-porous -- coverage is consistent across conditions
Spot priming bare vinyl areas only -- not full window surface
Typical bare exposure: 10-30% of total window surface at failure points
Clean vinyl surface before application -- no sanding required for bonding primer

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_S.notes: Finish coat on small exterior window. Coverage equivalent to NC COV_XWIN_FINISH (375 SF/gal) because substrate condition after prep/prime is equivalent to NC after prime. Brush has minimal waste; spray adds 20-40% waste.

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_M.notes: Finish coat on medium exterior window. Calibration baseline. 2 coats standard (all QT). TDL muntin windows have ~20% more surface area -- lower effective ea_per_gallon.

ITM_WINDOW_EXT_L.notes: Finish coat on large exterior window. Bay/bow windows consume proportionally more material due to multi-sash geometry and increased detail.

spray_waste_factor.notes: Spray waste 20-40% per Exterior_Application_Methods_Doctrine. Window profiles (3D sash, muntin intersections) cause higher overspray than flat trim.

coverage_profiles.notes: Finish coat coverage on prepped/primed exterior window surfaces. Coverage rate (375 SF/gal) matches NC exterior window finish (SYS_EXT_WIN_FINISH_STANDARD at 375 SF/gal, SYS_EXT_WIN_FINISH_PREMIUM at 350 SF/gal). Using 375 SF/gal as representative across all finish tiers for estimation. 2 coats standard at all QT.
assumptions: Prepped and primed surface -- coverage equivalent to NC after prime
Medium window: ~16 SF painted surface equivalent
Two-coat system standard at all quality tiers
TDL muntin windows have ~20% more surface area
Spray adds 20-40% waste factor for overspray

consumables.name: RP Assessment Kit (adhesion + chalk + moisture test)
consumables.specification: Cross-hatch cutter, pressure-sensitive tape (ASTM D3359), white cloth for chalk rub test, moisture meter, rot probe tool, mineral spirits
consumables.notes: RP-specific assessment supplies. One kit per project. Includes ASTM D3359 cross-hatch adhesion test materials, white cloth for chalk rub test (exterior-specific), moisture meter for wood sill/bottom rail MC readings, rot probe for end grain assessment. Shared across exterior RP specs. No coating ID solvent test needed for exterior windows (RC-003 -- exterior paint is predominantly acrylic latex).

consumables.name: Angled sash brush 1.5-2.5 inch
consumables.specification: Nylon/polyester blend angled sash brush, 1.5 inch for muntin detail, 2 inch for sash/frame
consumables.notes: Primary applicator for exterior window painting. 1.5 inch for muntin detail and sash rabbets. 2-2.5 inch for frame and sash faces. Quality nylon/polyester blend for acrylic exterior coatings. Replace when bristles lose precision -- critical for 1/16-inch glass lap. Yield: ~8 medium windows per brush before replacement.

consumables.name: Masking tape (exterior grade UV-resistant 14-day)
consumables.specification: UV-resistant exterior masking tape, 14-day clean removal rating
consumables.notes: UV-resistant exterior masking tape for glass masking, sill protection, casing protection. 14-day removal rating minimum for multi-day exterior projects. One roll (~60 yd) covers ~6 medium windows (glass perimeter + sill + casing edge). Consumed in setup and removed in cleanup.

consumables.name: Masking paper / kraft paper 12-18 inch
consumables.notes: For sill protection, casing protection, and glass masking when combined with tape. One roll covers ~10 medium windows. Also used for siding masking during spray application.

consumables.name: Masking film with tape edge (pre-taped poly)
consumables.specification: Pre-taped plastic film for glass masking, various widths
consumables.notes: Pre-taped plastic film for glass masking. Faster than paper/tape combo for single-lite windows. Primary masking method for standard windows (non-TDL). One roll covers ~8 medium windows. Also used for siding masking during spray.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 150 grit
consumables.notes: For feather-edge sanding after scraping on failing/peeling surfaces. Feather sanding is MANDATORY whenever scraping occurs. One sheet covers ~2 medium windows worth of feathering. Also used for adhesion scuff on sound paint.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 180 grit
consumables.notes: For light scuff sanding on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT prep and aluminum cladding scuff before DTM primer. Finer grit than 150 for adhesion tooth without surface damage. Also used for interstage sanding between coats.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit
consumables.notes: For QT4 interstage sanding between finish coats and QT5 interstage between all coats. Also for aluminum cladding scuff-sand (180-220 grit range). Fine grit for smooth finish preparation.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 320 grit
consumables.notes: QT5 only. For final interstage hand-sand before last finish coat. Ultra-fine grit for near-zero defect tolerance at QT5. One sheet per ~4 medium windows.

consumables.name: Tack cloth for dust removal
consumables.specification: Resin-impregnated tack cloth for dust pickup
consumables.notes: Remove sanding dust before prime or finish coat application. Critical at QT4/QT5 where dust nibs are visible in semi-gloss/gloss finish. One cloth per ~4 medium windows.

consumables.name: Liquid Sander / Deglosser
consumables.specification: Liquid sander/deglosser for chemical degloss, Krud Kutter Gloss-Off or equivalent
consumables.notes: RP-specific: chemical degloss for existing semi-gloss/gloss exterior window paint on SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT. Dulls existing sheen to promote adhesion without full mechanical sanding. One quart covers ~15 medium exterior windows (larger surface area per window than interior). Especially useful on complex window profiles where mechanical sanding cannot reach all recessed areas. Shared across RP specs.

consumables.name: Paintable exterior acrylic-latex or polymer caulk
consumables.specification: Exterior-grade paintable caulk (polyurethane, hybrid MS polymer, or acrylic-latex). NEVER silicone.
consumables.notes: For caulk assessment and repair per 'Think Like a Water Drop' protocol. Frame-to-casing, sill-to-casing, glass lap line repairs. NEVER use silicone -- prevents paint adhesion. One tube covers ~8 medium windows at typical RP caulk failure rate. More caulk consumption at FAIR/POOR conditions. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Glazing Compound (Exterior-Grade Acrylic or DAP 33)
consumables.specification: Exterior-grade glazing compound, DAP 33 or acrylic glazing compound
consumables.notes: Window-specific RP consumable for spot repair of failed glazing compound on older wood windows. Exterior glazing failure is more common than interior due to UV hardening and weather exposure. Scope-limited to <25% of glazing perimeter per window -- extensive failure is a separate glazier scope. Allow 3-7 day cure before priming. Modern IG units have no exposed glazing -- not needed for aluminum-clad or vinyl-clad IG windows.

consumables.name: Glass Scraper (Single-Edge Razor)
consumables.specification: Single-edge razor scraper for glass cleaning, retractable safety handle
consumables.notes: For post-cure glass cleanup. Razor scrape excess paint beyond 1/16-inch glass lap line. Used after final coat dries. One scraper lasts ~20 windows before blade replacement needed. Transfers from NC window spec (TSK_XWIN_GLASS_CLEANUP). Replace blade when dragging or scratching.

consumables.name: Carbide Scraper (Exterior Paint Scraping)
consumables.specification: Carbide scraper with replaceable blades, rigid and flexible profiles
consumables.notes: Exterior-specific tool for scraping failing/peeling paint on window frames, sashes, and sills. Carbide blades last longer than steel on exterior paint buildup. Rigid profile for flat surfaces, flexible for sash rabbets and muntin profiles. One scraper covers ~15 medium windows worth of scraping. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Canvas drop cloths
consumables.specification: Heavy-duty canvas drop cloth, minimum 4 oz weight
consumables.notes: For landscape and hardscape ground protection below window work areas. Catches scraping debris, power wash runoff, and paint drips. Reusable. Non-slip for crew traffic. Also used for walkway runners. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: 6-Mil Poly Sheeting (RRP Containment)
consumables.specification: Polyethylene sheeting 6 mil clear or black, 10 ft x 100 ft rolls
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL: pre_1978 = true AND lead_positive = true. 6-mil poly for ground containment extending 10 ft from structure per EPA RRP rule (40 CFR 745). Per-elevation quantity. Heavier gauge than standard protection -- must contain lead paint debris. Windows are HIGH RISK for lead (friction surfaces). Shared across all exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Mildewcide / Biocide Solution
consumables.specification: Mildewcide / biocide concentrate, mix per manufacturer directions
consumables.notes: For mildew/algae treatment on exterior window surfaces. North-facing and shaded windows are most susceptible. Apply during power wash or as separate treatment, allow 24 hr before priming. One quart of concentrate covers ~20 medium windows. Shared across exterior RP specs.

consumables.name: Wood Hardener / Consolidant
consumables.specification: Penetrating wood hardener/consolidant, epoxy or acrylic resin based
consumables.notes: For surface-softened wood at sill nose, sash bottom rail, and end grain areas. Penetrates and stabilizes surface-softened (not structurally compromised) wood. Apply to affected areas, allow full cure (24 hr) before sanding and priming. Structural rot is a HARD STOP (carpentry scope). One quart covers ~15 medium windows worth of spot treatment. Shared across exterior RP specs.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint with verified adhesion -- skip prime entirely
compatibility_rules.notes: Existing paint is sound and adhesion verified via ASTM D3359. No primer needed. Degloss/scuff existing surface and proceed to 2 finish coats. Most common exterior window repaint scenario (cosmetic refresh, color change). QT5 overrides this rule -- see COMPAT_XWRP_012.

compatibility_rules.description: Chalking surface -- chalk-binding primer mandatory (all claddings)
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY. Topcoat adhesion failure guaranteed without chalk-binding step. Full surface application required regardless of cladding type. Applies after power wash and 24-48 hour dry time.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing/peeling paint on wood -- acrylic stain-block primer
compatibility_rules.notes: Acrylic stain-block primer on bare wood areas. Spot prime when bare <30%; full prime when bare >=30% or SS_EXT_PEELING. Seal all exposed end-grain at sash edges and sill nose.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing/peeling paint on aluminum-clad -- DTM corrosion-inhibiting primer on exposed aluminum
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY on exposed bare aluminum. Corrosion-inhibiting DTM primer prevents oxidation under topcoat. Must scuff-sand bare aluminum (180-220 grit) before application. Spot prime exposed areas only. Also requires general RP primer (acrylic or chalk-binding) on painted areas if those areas also need prime.

compatibility_rules.description: Failing/peeling paint on vinyl-clad -- PVC bonding primer on exposed vinyl
compatibility_rules.notes: MANDATORY on exposed bare vinyl. Standard primers will NOT bond to vinyl -- peeling within 6-12 months. Clean vinyl surface before application. Recoat within 1 week or bonding primer loses flexibility. Spot prime exposed areas. Also requires general RP primer on painted areas if needed.

compatibility_rules.description: Low-E glass -- tape-and-film masking ONLY, no liquid mask
compatibility_rules.notes: HARD CONSTRAINT. Low-E coating is permanently damaged by liquid mask chemicals (scoring during removal). Low-E = tape-and-film masking ONLY, including individual pane tape-and-film for TDL windows (highest masking labor). Transfers unchanged from NC spec.

compatibility_rules.description: Vinyl-clad with dark color (LRV <55) -- VinylSafe IR-reflective finish required

then.notes: Solar-reflective IR coating is NON-NEGOTIABLE for vinyl with dark colors

compatibility_rules.notes: GATE CONDITION. Standard dark paint on vinyl causes thermal distortion (warping, buckling). VinylSafe IR-reflective coating technology drops surface temperature 20-30 deg F. Without VinylSafe, LRV must be 55+ to avoid damage. Transfers unchanged from NC spec.
Gloss finish reveals every surface imperfection and requires the maximum prep quality (QT5 interstage sanding protocol, near-zero defect tolerance). Only available at QT5.

compatibility_rules.description: Pre-1978 with paint disturbance -- RRP supplies and containment required
compatibility_rules.notes: EPA RRP Rule (40 CFR 745). Pre-1978 exterior paint is almost always lead. Windows are HIGH RISK (friction surfaces are the #1 residential lead dust generator). 6-mil poly ground containment extending 10 ft from structure. Wet scraping methods. HEPA vacuum. Lead-safe disposal. RRP modifier 2.0x on prep tasks involving paint disturbance.

compatibility_rules.description: Chalking on aluminum-clad -- chalk-binding primer takes precedence; DTM on any bare aluminum spots

then.notes: Chalk-binding is primary (full surface). If any bare aluminum is exposed, spot DTM primer first, then chalk-binding over remaining chalking surface.

compatibility_rules.notes: Dual primer scenario. Chalk-binding addresses the chalking condition. DTM addresses any exposed aluminum substrate. DTM applied first at bare spots, chalk-binding applied over remaining chalking areas.

compatibility_rules.description: Chalking on vinyl-clad -- chalk-binding primer takes precedence; PVC bonding on any bare vinyl spots

then.notes: Chalk-binding is primary (full surface). If any bare vinyl is exposed, spot PVC bonding primer first, then chalk-binding over remaining chalking surface.

compatibility_rules.notes: Dual primer scenario. Chalk-binding addresses the chalking condition. PVC bonding addresses any exposed vinyl substrate. PVC bonding applied first at bare spots, chalk-binding applied over remaining chalking areas.

compatibility_rules.description: QT5 -- 2-coat primer system regardless of condition
compatibility_rules.notes: QT5 requires 2-coat primer system with interstage sanding between all coats for maximum film build and surface quality. Even SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT gets primer at QT5 for system build. Follows SF_TRIM_EXT_RP QT5 pattern (COMPAT_TRRP_017).

compatibility_rules.description: Glazing compound repair scope limit -- <25% of perimeter

then.exceeds_scope: Refer to glazier -- separate scope item

compatibility_rules.notes: Glazing compound repair within this spec is limited to spot repair (<25% of perimeter). Extensive glazing failure exceeds painting scope -- refer to glazier. Modern IG units have no exposed glazing compound. Allow 3-7 day cure of new glazing before priming.

compatibility_rules.description: Sound paint with marginal adhesion -- spot prime with acrylic stain-block
compatibility_rules.notes: When sound paint has marginal adhesion test results, full prime is required as adhesion insurance. Scuff/degloss existing surface and apply full coat of acrylic primer before finish coats.

compatibility_rules.description: Rot detected at wood surfaces -- HARD STOP for affected area

then.reason: Structural wood damage (rot) outside painting scope. Refer to carpenter/contractor for replacement.

compatibility_rules.notes: Rot is most common at sill nose, sash bottom rail, and end grain areas. Painting over rot is cosmetic-only and fails within one season. Affected area is excluded from estimation -- remaining sound areas proceed normally. Surface-softened (not structurally compromised) wood may be treated with CON_WOOD_HARDENER.
